from worker import Worker
from provider import Provider

class ObservedProvider(Provider):
    def __init__(self, fail_after_delivery=False):
        super().__init__()
        self.attempts = 0
        self.fail_after_delivery = fail_after_delivery
    def send(self, body, idempotency_key):
        self.attempts += 1
        super().send(body, idempotency_key)
        if self.fail_after_delivery and self.attempts == 1:
            raise RuntimeError('simulated response loss after delivery')

worker = Worker()
job = 'confirmation-123'

provider = ObservedProvider()
for _ in range(3):
    worker.process(job, provider, lambda job: None)
assert provider.attempts == 3 and provider.delivered == {job: job}
print('Repeated logical job: 3 send attempts, 1 modeled delivery')

provider = ObservedProvider()
acks = []
def fail_ack(job):
    raise RuntimeError('simulated acknowledgment failure')
try:
    worker.process(job, provider, fail_ack)
except RuntimeError:
    pass
assert provider.delivered == {job: job}
worker.process(job, provider, acks.append)
assert provider.attempts == 2 and provider.delivered == {job: job} and acks == [job]
print('Acknowledgment failure after delivery, then retry: 2 send attempts, 1 modeled delivery')

provider = ObservedProvider(fail_after_delivery=True)
acks = []
try:
    worker.process(job, provider, acks.append)
except RuntimeError:
    pass
assert provider.delivered == {job: job} and acks == []
worker.process(job, provider, acks.append)
assert provider.attempts == 2 and provider.delivered == {job: job} and acks == [job]
print('Provider response loss after delivery, then retry: 2 send attempts, 1 modeled delivery')

first, restarted = Provider(), Provider()
worker.process(job, first, lambda job: None)
worker.process(job, restarted, lambda job: None)
assert sum(len(p.delivered) for p in (first, restarted)) == 2
print('Boundary control, fresh provider state on retry: 2 modeled deliveries across separate instances')
